done: ax3 patched to emit a default constructor when an AS3 class declares none. AS3 grants one implicitly, Haxe does not, so every generated class was unusable from hand-written code. Subclasses get new() { super(); }.
project.xml now puts the ax3 compat layer on the class path; generated code references ASAny and ASCompat, so any project consuming it needs them.
client dispatches packet 1778 (ObjectsMessageEvent) to the generated ObjectsMessageParser and reports the object count plus a five-object sample as DOM markers.
StuffData, ObjectMessageData and the room/engine parsers all reconverted with the patched converter.

blocked_on.what: adobe/serialization/json — JSONTokenizer and JSONEncoder will not lex
blocked_on.detail: ax3 rejects the escape sequences these two use. Guarded rules replaced the form-feed and doubled-backslash literals and the offsets moved, so the rewrite lands, but the lexer still refuses.
blocked_on.why_it_matters: StuffDataBase is the only consumer, and it needs JSONDecoder for legacy stuff data. Without it the furniture path does not compile.
blocked_on.decision_needed: PLAN.md already lists porting-or-dropping the vendored trees as an explicit decision. Haxe ships haxe.Json, so the clean option is to declare the Adobe library an exception and route StuffDataBase through haxe.Json. That is a behavioural change (strict mode, error text) and is the owner call, not mine.
